agent_notes: Blast radius: InstanceConfig is used by 9 production modules and 17 test modules. Its signature and fields do not change, and an empty URL (the default, and what routes.py:790 InstanceConfig() produces) still passes because validate_arr_url_config returns (True, '') when url is empty or blank.

Where the check runs: startup (config.py:371 ensure_config -> load_settings) and every in-process reload after a settings save (routes.py:1199, 1462, 1511, 1535). Those reloads re-read a TOML written from settings that already passed validation, so a mid-request failure is unlikely after a successful startup.

agent_notes: Do not ship yet: a concrete numeric-host bypass defeats the new metadata-address block. All 56 validator tests pass but miss this case.

findings.fix_hint: Reject noncanonical numeric IPv4 hosts or normalize them before applying the blocked-address checks. Add model-level regression tests for decimal, hexadecimal, and shortened IPv4 representations of blocked addresses.
findings.problem: InstanceConfig(url="http://2852039166", enabled=True) succeeds. The helper at triggarr/web/validation.py:150-173 treats this numeric host as an arbitrary hostname after ipaddress rejects it. Verified that HTTPX preserves the host and socket.getaddrinfo with AI_NUMERICHOST resolves it to 169.254.169.254 without DNS. Startup passes the accepted URL into the client at triggarr/startup.py:153-160, permitting requests to the metadata address this new check explicitly intends to block. This is a concrete bypass, independent of the documented DNS-rebinding exception.
